status: complete; verified for this codec scope

interfaces.FCompressUserString: Borrows non-NUL byte text and an actual writable byte span; returns optional encoded-byte count. No allocation; failure leaves output untouched.
interfaces.FDecompressUserString: Borrows encoded bytes and a character destination including NUL; returns optional decoded-byte count excluding NUL. Invalid bytes/capacity clear only the first byte of a nonempty destination.
interfaces.FDecompressUserStringBytes: Same bounded decode/size contract; deliberately permits CP1252/non-UTF-8 bytes at the narrow legacy race import boundary. Embedded decoded NUL remains invalid.
interfaces.FReadUserString: Borrows record bytes and actual text destination; returns optional record bytes consumed including marker and raw NUL, retaining raw/compressed admission and UTF-8 checks.
interfaces.FReadLegacyRaceString: The actual private legacy race reader also uses spans and an optional consumed-byte count; keeps its exact 32-byte field budget and the caller full-record-consumption check.

preserved_limits.compression: Original 1024-byte staging and nibble completion/padding boundaries retained: 2047 spaces can produce 1024 bytes; the next complete nibble pair still fails.
preserved_limits.decompression: Destination capacity includes NUL and remains at most 1024; encoded input retains the positive int16_t range. Existing callers preserve their logical output budgets within actual physical arrays/arena slices.
preserved_limits.names: Saved fields keep 31 UTF-8 bytes plus NUL. Compression budgets are unchanged; UTF-8 admission remains at the applicable record boundary.

callers.message_arena: The 0x800-byte UI arena is split through actual spans: compression uses its second half, and displayed text decoding uses its remaining tail with the existing 1000-byte text budget.
callers.validated_heap_copies: Read fleet names and replayed name orders copy validated UTF-8 plus NUL into the exact persistent allocation. Battle-plan decode copies into its actual fixed name field. No allocator, storage width, publication order or wire record changes.
